passage.text: When the commuters in our town started a cycle routes project, few residents expected it to grow so quickly. At first, the organisers met in a small room and planned one simple activity involving safe paths. They soon discovered that people were more willing to join when they could see a clear benefit for the neighbourhood. The organisers therefore published a short timetable and invited local businesses to offer practical help.

The project was not completely easy. Some volunteers were worried that the work would take too much time, while others wanted to change the plan every week. The team solved this by giving each person one small responsibility and reviewing the results together. This made the project feel manageable, and it also meant that new volunteers could contribute without special experience.

Looking back, the organiser says the most important lesson was not the final result but the way people learned to cooperate. The group still has problems, especially when the weather affects outdoor work, yet members now discuss solutions rather than blaming one another. For this reason, the project has become a useful example of how a modest local idea can create lasting connections.

parts.passageTitle: Part 4 – Volunteering at an animal shelter

passage.text: I started volunteering at an animal shelter during the school holidays last summer. (16) ..... The shelter cared for over fifty cats and dogs, and the staff were always busy looking after the animals. The shelter relied entirely on donations from the public and the hard work of volunteers, so every hour I spent there made a real difference to the animals and the staff.

My main job was cleaning the cages and refilling food and water bowls every morning. (17) ..... It was not a glamorous task, but I could see how much the animals appreciated the attention and care they received from the volunteers. I learned to be patient and gentle with frightened animals, understanding that they needed time to trust humans again after whatever difficult experiences they had been through.

One day, a young dog arrived who had been injured in a road accident and was very frightened. (18) ..... The vet came twice a week to check on his progress, and I was allowed to help during the treatments by holding the dog still. I sat with him for hours each day, speaking softly and offering treats until he began to trust me enough to let me touch him and check his injuries properly.

Watching the dog recover and eventually find a new home was incredibly rewarding for me. (19) ..... Seeing him leave with a caring family made all the hard work worthwhile and showed me the difference we can make. The experience of helping an injured animal recover and find a loving home gave me a sense of purpose and showed me that my efforts could have a direct impact on another creature.

Volunteering at the shelter completely changed my perspective on animal welfare and care. (20) ..... I now hope to become a veterinarian so I can help animals professionally and make a real difference in their lives. I also learned that animals need patience rather than attention all the time, because a quiet approach often helps a frightened animal feel safe enough to respond.
